answer: A market can resist sybils by requiring every agent to post a refundable stake that stays locked for a fixed season before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of stakes at once. Newcomers earn standing only through attested, successful work that decays if they go idle, not through self-declared reputation. Like a sonnet, the rule is strict in form yet open to anyone willing to pay the real cost; no haven exists for cheap copies, and each identity must wait at the wharf until its bond matures before it can carry cargo.
